correctness.rationale: In q=arctan(√κx)/√κ, the ODE becomes Hamiltonian q′=y, y′=−V′(q) with V(q)=κ^{-1}log sec(√κ q); the energy is L_A/(2κ), domain |q|<π/(2√κ) and every positive energy gives a closed oval. The inverted potential density g(v)=√κ/(e^{2κv}−1)^{1/2} is integrable with ∫g=h, giving T_A√L_A→2π. Uniform integral control of time primitives yields the triangular physical-time phase, hence the tangent pushforward Cauchy law. Direct dt/dx produces the stated exact density. After u=log(1+κx²), fixed-p absolute moments reduce to a beta integral for p<1, exactly 4√L/(T√κ) for p=1, and endpoint Laplace/Gamma integral for p>1, giving the claimed constants. **Presentation correction:** in RESULT.md Step 2 the bound I_E−Q_A stated for ∫_q^{Q_A} over possibly negative q is too small: the universal bound is 2(I_E−Q_A), still o(1), so its proof conclusion and theorem remain valid. Independent exact algebraic inspection rather than finite logs establishes limits. The inspected verify.py quadrature is only corroboration.
residual_risks: One displayed bound for the uniform phase-time primitive is missing a factor 2 when q ranges over negative values; the corrected 2(I_E−Q_A)=o(1) establishes exactly the needed conclusion without altering the final claim.

value.rationale: This provides an explicit nontrivial weak-limit law emerging from compact periodic orbits of a concrete cubic global center and a sharp moment-integrability phase transition, including constants and uniform time-phase behavior. Such occupation statistics are a natural dynamical invariant beyond existing center-classification and period monotonicity; the p=1 critical boundary and p>1 amplitudes distinguish weak convergence from uniform integrability.
residual_risks: All asymptotics require A→∞ for fixed κ>0 and fixed p; uniformity in p near1 or κ→0 is not established.

final_claim: For x′=(1+κx²)y,y′=−x, κ>0, the original-time occupation distribution on the amplitude-A periodic orbit has an explicit density and converges to centered Cauchy scale 1/√κ; all fixed-order absolute moments change regime exactly at p=1 with constants, and the canonical q=arctan(√κx)/√κ phase tends uniformly to a triangular wave while T_A√log(1+κA²)→2π.
limitations: Moment asymptotics are for fixed p and κ, not a joint critical or zero-κ limit.
Time is the original physical clock; reparameterized flows need not share the law.
